items.description: One look row — the appearance peer of WorldKit's way of moving. Every appearance a world offers is a row of this data, never a renderer branch; world.looks prints these names.

name.description: The look's stable kebab-case name, authored literally or through a Text state cell; it is unique within the definition and assignable by the look table.

source.description: Where the appearance resolves from (a catalog rig or a creation).

anyOf.description: The procedural humanoid catalog (WorldRigCatalog) — one look source among others.

index.description: The procedural renderer catalog rig to pin, or null for the occupant-owned pick. A fresh occupant seeds that pick from its first local slot and carries it across authority transfers, so ordinary admission does not restyle it.

anyOf.description: A sculpted creation worn by the body — resolved against the world's WorldPrototype rows.

prototypeId.description: The referenced Id, authored literally or through a Text state cell; it must resolve at validation.

scale.description: The uniform render scale. Appearance only — it does not resize the body's motion tuning or its collision volume.

motion.description: How the look animates with the body (see WorldLookMotion).

gaitAmplitude.description: The catalog rig's limb-swing scale (1 = the pre-look default; 0 stills the gait).

replayFrames.description: Whether a creation look replays its authored timeline on the render clock.

secondsPerFrame.description: The creation timeline cadence when ReplayFrames is set.

cues.description: The creation look's cues (see WorldLookCue); a firing cue's frame overrides the replay cursor for its hold.

items.description: One cue of a creation look: a named timeline frame the body holds for HoldSeconds when the cue fires — a blink, a twitch, a tail flick. A cue fires by itself on a semi-random interval drawn uniformly from MinSeconds..MaxSeconds (a deterministic presentation draw seeded by the body, never simulation state), and fires on demand through the stamp pool's TriggerCue door, which is how a face probe reading the player's own camera blinks the avatar in sync; a triggered cue re-arms the interval, so a driven cue never double-fires with the self schedule. Both interval bounds absent is a cue that fires only on demand.

holdSeconds.description: How long the frame holds, seconds.

minSeconds.description: The shortest rest between self-fires, seconds, or null with MaxSeconds for a cue that never self-fires.

maxSeconds.description: The longest rest between self-fires, seconds.

dynamics.description: The dynamics row a second-order follower drives the stamped ROOT through — the client's interpolated body pose is the target, the follower's output is what renders. null (the default) is today's behavior: the root follows the interpolated pose exactly, no lag.

partDynamics.description: A creation part id to dynamics row map — each named part follows the root's own resolved transform with its own personality, layered ON TOP of Dynamics. Legitimate only on a creation source (a catalog rig exports no parts); each key must name a part the creation's own part table declares.

assignment.description: The look→entity assignment policy — ABSENT resolves to Default.
